meta.notes: Market: India. Primary ICP is individual policyholders, who cannot be prospected as companies, so the 19 prospects target the secondary ICP (agents and small brokers); several are larger distributors or group-benefit brokers listed as channel partners outside the 1-10 size band. Contacts are left empty and no personal names are quoted. Forum evidence comes from a Reddit snapshot mirror (reddit.sentinel-team.org) and freefincal reader stories. Unfetchable (robots/403/timeouts): angelone.in, itbrief.in, cfotech.in, business-standard.com, policybazaar.com, newsmeter.in, producthunt.com (fairClaims by Policygaido), indiehackers.com, insurancesamadhan.in (timeout), beshak.org (429), policyholder.gov.in broker list, paybima.com, renewbuy.com, connect-brite.lovable.app (ClaimForSure). None are cited. No primary IRDAI notice specifically warning about fee-charging claim consultants was found; the 2020 notice cited is about fee-seeking impostors. The proportionate-deduction rule (ev-21) is from a non-official wiki and was not verified against the circular.

summary.statement: Health insurers received about 1.18 lakh Bima Bharosa complaints in FY26, and claim issues make up about 69% of general/health grievances.
Ombudsman complaints about partial or total repudiation rose to 35,186 in FY26, and the CIO says 95% of health complaints concern claim rejections.
Self-reported LocalCircles surveys put rejection or partial settlement at roughly 4 in 10 claimants, or more.
Against this, IRDAI data shows repudiations fell to about 8% of claims in FY25, top insurers settle 97-99% of claims by count, and Policybazaar reports 94% approval.
No public data breaks down how often specific clauses (room rent, sub-limits) are misapplied; IRDAI does not collect denial reasons.
Claimants escalate themselves: insurer grievance officer, then Bima Bharosa, then the Ombudsman, often over months (10 to 22 months in documented cases).
Frustrations reported include repeated document requests, template denials, unresponsive grievance channels and unclear process.
Distributor help can stop after a first reconsideration, leaving the claimant to escalate alone.
Policyholders find grievance mechanisms hard to use without guidance.
In aggregate, disallowed plus repudiated health claims reached about Rs 26,000 crore in FY24.
The average paid claim is about Rs 28,910; documented disputes range from about Rs 44,000 to Rs 2.48 lakh.
Most reimbursement claimants need financial aid to cover upfront payments.
There is no source for the typical size of a disputed deduction per family; the per-case value of a dispute is still unknown.
A paid success-fee market exists: Insurance Samadhan charged Rs 500 plus 9% of recovered amounts and reports INR 160 crore recovered.
Assisted resubmissions reverse far more rejections than DIY (32-67% vs 6%), and the Ombudsman rules for policyholders in a majority of cases.
Willingness to pay is capped by free routes: the Ombudsman charges nothing, and claimants do win alone.
Success-fee economics are narrow: the leading service accepts only 3-4 of every 100 cases, and the Ombudsman win rate fell to about 54% in FY26.
No evidence was found on what individuals would pay for a Rs 499-2,999 self-serve package.
Options in use include distributor claim desks (Policybazaar, Ditto, PolicyX, nyvo), success-fee services (Insurance Samadhan), free public escalation (Ombudsman), and general AI chatbots.
Assistance type changes outcomes, per Policybazaar's own data.
No evidence was found on how claimants compare or choose between these options.
Brokers employ claims staff to review TPA denials against policy terms and contest them, and to upload files and chase deficiencies by hand.
Rejected claims pull HR into escalations and hours of coordination with TPAs and insurers.
Group-health intermediaries (Plum, Loop, Onsurity, Nova, Pazcare) already compete on claims handling, so they are both potential buyers and incumbents.
No evidence was found that is specific to individual agents or POSPs.
Practitioner guidance treats AI as a drafting aid that can invent citations, and recommends a lawyer for complex, high-value cases.
Poorly drafted complaints can lose winnable cases, so an incorrect analysis has a real cost.
No evidence was found on the accuracy level users expect.

Distributors (Policybazaar, Ditto, PolicyX, nyvo) provide claim help, mainly to customers who bought through them.
Paid success-fee services such as Insurance Samadhan handle selected disputes.
For group health, broker claims teams and HR handle disputes manually.
AI tools are emerging: pre-claim policy-gap analysis (Policygaido) and generic chatbots for drafting complaints.
